textbookText: If a force is applied on a system or on a particle, and displacement is caused in the direction of the force, then work done, W = Fd If the force makes an angle θ with the displacement, we consider the effective part of the force in the direction of the displacement, known as the component of the force Fcosθ. Therefore, the work done, W, is calculated as W = Fcosθd = Fdcosθ. Hence W = Fd cosθ is the general formula. If θ = 0, then W = Fd i.e F and d act in the same direction. If θ = 900, then W = 0 as cos900 = 0 Up to this point, the examples we have studied are all the instances of work done by a constant force.

b. Work Done by a Variable Force

In this case, the value of the force applied to do work isn’t constant. Either the magnitude, the direction of the force, or both change. The force acting on a spring is an example of a variable force, where the force changes with the extension produced in the wire. Other examples include magnetic force, electrostatic force, and gravitational force. The work done by a variable force can be analyzed both analytically and graphically.
